title: SPA/263/2021 of NEERAJ KUMAR Vs CHIEF EDUCATION OFFICER HARIDWAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN
AND
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
SPECIAL APPEAL No. 263 OF 2021
04TH OCTOBER, 2021
Between:
Neeraj Kumar.
 ...Appellant
and
Chief Education Officer and others.

: Mr. Vipul Sharma, the learned counsel.
Counsel for the respondent nos. 1
and 2.
: Mr. S.S. Chauhan, the learned Deputy
Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand.
The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT : (per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Sri Raghvendra Singh Chauhan)
 Aggrieved by the order dated 23.06.2021,
passed by a learned Single Judge, in Writ Petition (M/S)
No. 1124 of 2021, the appellant has preferred the
present Special Appeal. By the said order, the learned
Single Judge had disposed of the Writ Petition filed by

2
the appellant-writ petitioner with a direction to the
Director, School Education, Uttarakhand to consider and
decide the appeal filed by the expelled members of the
General Body of the Society, which runs the Institution,
as early as possible, but not later than four months from
the date of production of a certified copy of the order. It
was further observed that the petitioner shall also be
given an opportunity of hearing while deciding the said
appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall
be referred to as arrayed in the Writ Petition.
3. In the Writ Petition, the petitioner had sought
a direction to the respondent no. 3 to initiate the
process for the General Body of the CMD Inter-College
("the College", for short), for inducting members for
constitution of the Committee of Management of the
College, and to handover the charge to the duly elected
Committee of Management.
4. Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that
the petitioner is a farmer, and is engaged in agricultural
activities to earn his livelihood. Further, the petitioner,

3
in earlier years, had acquired membership of the
General Body of the College, and had made his
contribution towards the betterment of the College. In
the recent years, frivolous proceedings for including
members were initiated by one person or the other.
Consequently, there had been a gross mismanagement
in the Committee of Management. Considering such
anomalies and financial irregularities in the day to day
activities of the College, one member of the General
Body of the College, namely Satyapal Tyagi, had
preferred a complaint before the Hon'ble Cabinet
Minister of the State. Consequently, the Hon'ble Cabinet
Minister had directed the competent authority to carry
out a thorough inquiry into the matter.
5. When such orders for enquiry were passed,
initially, the Committee of Management contested such
action, and challenged the order passed by the Hon'ble
Cabinet Minister. Consequently, Writ Petition (M/S) No.
2562 of 2019 was also filed before this Court, wherein
the issue, with regard to the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble
Cabinet Minister to order an inquiry was also raised. In
the said Writ Petition, no interim order was passed.
During the pendency of the said Writ Petition, the

4
inquiry proceedings culminated, and finally by order
dated 19.11.2019 the Writ Petition was dismissed as
withdrawn by this Court.
6. The Inquiry Committee had dealt with each
and every allegation, and had taken into consideration
the version of the complainant, and the version of the
persons against whom the allegations were made.
Ultimately, the Inquiry Committee concluded that since
2010, gross illegalities have been committed while
inducting the members in the year 2010, i.e. with
respect to the 100 life-members; the same was directed
to be cancelled. Similarly the membership of twenty-one members, who were inducted in the year 2012, was
also directed to be cancelled. Further, the membership
of eighty-seven members, of the list dated 14.08.2019,
was also directed to be cancelled.
7. With respect to the financial irregularities,
again a specific inquiry was carried out. The Inquiry
Committee concluded that there are serious allegations
of financial irregularities and misappropriation. The
Inquiry Committee directed that the allegations are
required to be further inquired by the Accountant

5
General/Audit Team. It was further directed that the
requisite records of the school be sealed, so that further
interpolation may not be carried out in the records.
8. In the meantime the Inquiry Committee had
submitted its report before the competent authority, in
which the allegations, regarding gross violation in
inducting the members of the general body, were
substantiated. Pursuant to the said recommendations
made by the Inquiry Committee, on 30.01.2020, the
Chief Education Officer, Haridwar passed an order,
whereby the membership of eighty-seven members of
the list dated 14.08.2019, which were not found to be
properly inducted, was directed to be cancelled.
Resultantly, only two valid members remained in the
General Body. Since most of the members were not
found to be properly inducted, on 21.12.2019, the
Principal of the CMD Inter College, Chudiyal, Haridwar
was initially appointed as an Authorized Controller for
the College. Subsequently, by the order dated
21.11.2020, the Deputy Education Officer, Bhagwanpur,
Haridwar, was appointed as an Authorized Controller for
the College. The Authorized Controller still continues.

6
9. Those members, whose membership was
cancelled, were aggrieved by the order dated
30.01.2020. Therefore, they filed an appeal before the
Director, School Education, Uttarakhand, challenging the
cancellation of their membership. The said appeal
continues to be pending before the Director, School
Education, Uttarakhand.
10. According to the petitioner, the provisions
regarding the appointment of the Authorized Controller
are contained in Section 34(4) of the Uttaranchal School
Education Act, 2006 ("the Act" for short). Section 34(4)
of the Act makes it absolutely clear that the appointment
of the Authorized Controller cannot be continued beyond
a limited period. Moreover, the Authorized Controller
cannot be continued beyond November, 2021. Further,
he is under an obligation to act in accordance with the
scheme of administration of the College. In the case of
appointment of the Authorized Controller, as per the
provisions contained in the scheme of administration,
the process to induct members shall be concluded within
a period of six months. The scheme of administration
provides that the process of inducting members shall be
completed within a period of six months, and it would be

7
a natural consequence that, once the members are
formed, the process of election, and constitution of the
Committee of Management, shall also be initiated.
11. In the present case though the Authorized
Controller had already been appointed, but no steps
have been taken to induct any members within the
stipulated period of six months, as provided in the
scheme of administration. Further, the Authorized
Controller, who had been appointed by the order dated
21.12.2019, cannot sit idle. He is under an obligation to
start the process of induction of members, and to
carefully start the election process, and to constitute the
Committee of Management.
12. It is further pleaded by the petitioners that the
inaction and omission on the part of the respondent
authorities, more particularly the Authorized Controller,
to initiate the process of election is absolutely erroneous
and contrary to provisions contained in the law. In this
regard, the petitioner had also made a representation to
the respondent no. 3, a copy whereof was also
forwarded to the respondent nos. 1 and 2. However, till
2015 no action had been taken. The Authorized

8
Controller cannot be appointed for such an indefinite
period just to sit idle, and the respondent-authorities are
under an obligation to take recourse to law.
13. Aggrieved by the omission on part of the
respondents, the petitioner filed a Writ Petition before a
learned Single Judge of this Court. However, by the
order dated 23.06.2021, the learned Single Judge has
disposed of the Writ Petition as aforesaid. Hence, the
present Special Appeal before this Court
14. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, the learned Deputy
Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand, has
raised the following contentions before this Court :-
 Firstly, both the Writ Petition and the present
Special Appeal are highly misconceived. For, according
to the petitioner himself, he is no longer a member of
the General Body of the College. Despite the fact that
his membership was cancelled by the order dated
30.01.2020, he has not filed any appeal before the
Director, School Education. Therefore, presently, he is a
person alien to the College.

9
 Secondly, the Writ Petition is not a Public
Interest Litigation.
 Thirdly, the order passed by the learned
Single Judge, directing the Director, School Education, to
decide the appeal filed by the expelled members of the
General Body of the Society, which runs the institution,
as early as possible, is an innocuous order. Therefore,
the petitioner cannot be aggrieved by the same.
 Lastly, the Authorized Controller's tenure is till
November, 2021. Therefore, ample time does exist for
the Authorized Controller to take the necessary steps for
inducting new members, and for holding the necessary
election, and to constitute the Committee of
Management. Therefore, the Writ Petition and the
present Special Appeal are premature in their nature.
15. This Court has asked a pointed query to Mr.
Vipul Sharma, the learned counsel for the petitioner :
whether the petitioner continues to be a member of the
General Body of the Society, or not? Mr. Vipul Sharma
has frankly conceded that the petitioner is no longer a
member of the General Body of the Society. According

10
to him, the petitioner's membership was cancelled by
the order dated 30.01.2020.
16. This Court has also asked a pointed query to
the learned counsel for the petitioner whether the
petitioner has filed any appeal before the Director,
School Education, challenging the order dated
30.01.2020. To this query, the learned counsel has
again frankly conceded that no such appeal has been
filed by the petitioner.
17. The learned counsel for the petitioner further
submits that the learned Single Judge has granted a
relief never prayed for by the petitioner. For, the
petitioner had sought a direction to the Authorized
Controller to induct members for the General Body of
the College, to constitute the Committee of
Management, and to handover the charge to the duly
elected Committee of Management. Therefore, the
impugned order deserves to be set-aside by this Court.
18. Considering these aspects, it is obvious that
the petitioner is an alien to the functioning of the
Society, and to the running of the College. However,

11
interestingly, the petitioner has not filed the Writ Petition
as a Public Interest Litigation. Therefore, the
contention, raised by Mr. S.S. Chauhan, the learned
Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand,
that the Writ Petition and the Special Appeal are not
even maintainable, necessarily has to be accepted. For,
it is a settled principle of law that busy bodies cannot be
permitted to invoke the writ jurisdiction of this Court.
19. Although, Mr. Vipul Sharma, the learned
counsel for the petitioner, has pleaded that the learned
Single Judge has granted a relief never prayed for, it is a
settled principle of law that a relief can be moulded by
the Court considering the facts and circumstances of the
case. Therefore, the learned Single Judge was justified
in taking a holistic view of the case, and issuing the
necessary direction to the Director, School Education.
20. Since the College was running without a
Committee of Management, since the tenure of the
Authorized Controller was due to come to an end, and
since there were only two members left in the General
Body, the learned Single Judge was justified in directing
the Director, School Education, to decide the appeal filed

12
by the expelled members of the General Body of the
Society within four months from the date of the
production of the certified copy of the order. Therefore,
this Court does not find any illegality or perversity in the
impugned order.
21. For the reasons stated above, this Court does
not find any merit in the present Special Appeal. It is,
hereby, dismissed.
22. No order as to costs.

_____________________________
RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN, C.J.
___________________
ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Dt: 04th October, 2021
Rahul
